Design 3's bump sustained itself at rest in bright light (self 5, neighbours 2.5, bias -3.5), and lowering the bias enough to stop that also stopped bumps forming in bright light. Here the copy E ends each bump: E -> every wall node -3, and R2's drive +4 -> +7, so during a run the net push is ~+4 (R2 7 minus E ~3 x 0.7-1), and when R2 drops (tau 2) E lingers (tau 4) and pulls the wall down for a few ticks. Wall bias -3.5 -> -3.7. Benched with a fixed-bias E: pull 0.64-0.89 by tick 40-79 at light 0.03-8, the bump gone 10-20 ticks after the drive stops at every level, resting beat 0.002-0.019. E's bias still follows Dm (-2.3 - 8 Dm), so in dim light E is weaker during runs: more net drive where bumps form slowest, and a weaker kill where bumps die anyway. Everything else is design 3's. Expected in probes: steady light running ~30-40% in dim light and ~10% in bright, as bumps that pull ~0.6-0.85 once formed and stop when R2 does; no beating at rest beyond ~0.02; ramps mostly pulling, falls mostly not.
